newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline rises on supply tightness.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline rises on supply tightness.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot CARB gasoline prices firmed midday as rumors of tight local supplies kept buyers scrambling for product ahead of inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) Tuesday.
Chevron's shut fluid catalytic cracker (FCC) and trimmed gasoline production at two major Los Angeles refineries, left traders worried about inadequate stocks.
Mobil, which reportedly sold off large cargoes of heavy crude following a late November fire, was seen buying product along with Texaco.
"They've sold crude which would put them in a position to buy products," a trader said. "Little guys wouldn't scare this market up," he said, citing hikes in wholesale prices for CARB gasoline.
Chevron's FCC is expected to restart by December 25, a source said.
Bids for CARB gasoline rose 0.75 cents a gallon to 70.75 cents, despite a 2.02-cent collapse in the January futures contract.
"It's a conflict between local fundamentals and what the NYMEX is doing," a broker said.
Bids for conventional gas eased 0.50 cent to 68 cents a gallon.
Distillates were mostly lower, with CARB diesel down half a cent to 72.50/73.50 cents a gallon. Low sulphur diesel in L.A. remained flat 69/70 cents a gallon.
